title: Retries with exponential backoff and jitter
prompt:
The reading app's background worker calls a flaky text-to-speech API. Write the retry helper it uses.

  • backoffDelay(attempt, { baseMs, maxMs, random }): the wait before retry number attempt (0 for the first retry). Use full jitter: random() * min(maxMs, baseMs * 2 ** attempt), where random returns a number in [0, 1).
  • async retryWithBackoff(fn, { retries, baseMs, maxMs, random, sleep }): calls await fn(attempt) with attempt = 0, 1, 2... Returns the first successful result. On an error, if retries remain and the error is retryable, it await sleep(backoffDelay(...)) and tries again. After retries failed retries (so retries + 1 calls total), it throws the last error.
  • An error with err.retryable === false (think HTTP 400: retrying won't help) is thrown immediately with no sleep.

random and sleep are injected so the tests are deterministic and instant. Example with baseMs: 100, maxMs: 1000, random: () => 1: waits are 100, 200, 400, 800, 1000, 1000...

tests.name: delay doubles each attempt and is capped at maxMs
tests.code:
const o = { baseMs: 100, maxMs: 1000, random: () => 1 };
assertEqual([0,1,2,3,4,5].map(a => backoffDelay(a, o)), [100, 200, 400, 800, 1000, 1000]);

tests.name: full jitter scales the delay by random()
returns immediately on success without sleeping
retries transient failures, then succeeds
gives up after retries and throws the last error
does not retry errors marked retryable: false
retries: 0 means exactly one call

hints: Write backoffDelay first: the "ceiling" is Math.min(maxMs, baseMs * 2 ** attempt), and full jitter picks a random point below it.
In the catch block, decide whether to give up before sleeping. Give up if attempt >= retries or err.retryable === false.
Shape: for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) { try { return await fn(attempt); } catch (err) { if (attempt >= retries || err.retryable === false) throw err; await sleep(backoffDelay(attempt, opts)); } }
explain:
This is the exact policy AWS recommends ("exponential backoff and full jitter") and that most SDKs, including the AWS and Anthropic clients, use in some form. Exponential growth gives a struggling service room to recover; the cap keeps a single job from waiting forever; jitter spreads 10,000 clients that failed at the same instant across the whole window instead of having them hammer the server again in lockstep (a retry storm or thundering herd).

In an interview: "Retries only for transient errors (timeouts, 429, 503), exponential backoff with full jitter and a cap, a small retry budget, and only on idempotent operations or with an idempotency key. After the last retry, the message goes to a dead-letter queue."
